knowledge:
- key_parameters: region=A data.frame specifying user-defined mutable positions (in amino acid positions) corresponding to the DNA sequences. If specified in input_seq(), mutations are restricted to these regions ;; keep=Logical parameter in codon_random() and dinu_to(). If TRUE, retains the original codon usage bias/pattern ;; n=Numeric parameter in codon_random() controlling the proportion of codons allowed to be mutated (e.g., 0.5 for 50%) ;; max.codon/min.codon=String specifying the codon to maximize or minimize in codon_to() ;; max.dinu/min.dinu=String specifying the dinucleotide to maximize or minimize in dinu_to() ;; alt=Target codon usage pattern in codon_mimic(), specified as either a codon usage vector (from get_cu) or a DNAStringSet of length 1
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation
- when_to_use: When designing recombinant virus sequences or other gene constructs to study the biological effects of codon usage bias or dinucleotide usage bias while keeping the translated amino acid sequence identical
- pitfalls: If the region parameter is not specified in the regioned_dna object, downstream mutation functions will mutate the entire sequence, which might disrupt conserved regions. Additionally, the region file must specify mutable positions in amino acid positions, not nucleotide positions.

workflows.name: synonymous_mutation_design
workflows.intent: Design synonymously mutated DNA sequences with customized codon or dinucleotide usage patterns while preserving amino acid sequences and optional conserved regions.
input: regions.csv (optional CSV file specifying mutable amino acid positions)
workflows.stages: 1. Import sequences and define mutable regions using input_seq to create a regioned_dna object. ;; 2. Retrieve baseline sequence properties (optional) using get_dna, get_region, get_cu, get_du, get_nu, get_freq, or get_rscu. ;; 3. Generate synonymous mutations using one of the mutation functions: codon_random (random mutations), codon_to (maximize/minimize specific codons), dinu_to (maximize/minimize specific dinucleotides), or codon_mimic (mimic a target codon usage pattern). ;; 4. Export the mutated DNA sequences using get_dna and Biostrings::writeXStringSet.
workflows.code:
library("SynMut")
filepath.fasta <- system.file("extdata", "example.fasta", package = "SynMut")
filepath.csv <- system.file("extdata", "target_regions.csv", package = "SynMut")
region <- read.csv(filepath.csv)
rgd.seq <- input_seq(filepath.fasta, region)
rgd.seq
get_dna(rgd.seq)
str(get_region(rgd.seq))
get_region(input_seq(filepath.fasta))
get_cu(rgd.seq)
get_du(rgd.seq)
get_nu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- codon_random(rgd.seq)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- codon_random(rgd.seq, keep = TRUE)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- codon_random(rgd.seq, n = 0.5)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- codon_to(rgd.seq, max.codon = "AAC")
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- codon_to(rgd.seq, min.codon = "AAC")
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- dinu_to(rgd.seq, max.dinu = "cg")
get_du(mut.seq) - get_du(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- dinu_to(rgd.seq, min.dinu = "CA")
get_du(mut.seq) - get_du(rgd.seq)
mut.seq <- dinu_to(rgd.seq, max.dinu = "cg", keep = TRUE)
get_du(mut.seq) - get_du(rgd.seq)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
target <- get_cu(rgd.seq)[2,]
mut.seq <- codon_mimic(rgd.seq, alt = target)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
target <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet("TTGAAAA-CTC-N--AAG")
mut.seq <- codon_mimic(rgd.seq, alt = target)
get_cu(mut.seq) - get_cu(rgd.seq)
get_freq(mut.seq) - get_freq(rgd.seq)
get_rscu(mut.seq) - get_rscu(rgd.seq)
Biostrings::writeXStringSet(get_dna(rgd.seq), "rgd.fasta")
